rationale: VIRTUAL OVERRIDES WERE DEAD: registries on `this` were only initialized inside the base_class_clause branch of DERIVED classes, so base-class virtuals (walked earlier, top-down) were never registered and no Overrides edge could ever emit. Registration is unconditional now; resolution is post-loop and transitive. M14 ONTOLOGY (2026-10-04), the `override` KEYWORD: `Derived::run` is written `void run() override;`, which is not a shape to be matched — it is the author asserting that `run` overrides a base virtual. The resolver read the keyword only for the `decorators` payload, so the edge it produced carried `reasonCode: signature-match` at 0.9 and the strongest evidence C++ offers went unused. Measured over the corpus: 735 `override`-keyword sites against 185 `overrides` edges emitted. With the keyword wired in, this row is a FACT (confidence 1.0, reasonCode `override-keyword+signature-match`, and `overrideSpecifier` recorded so a reader can tell an asserted override from an inferred one without re-parsing). The signature-match path is unchanged for a method with NO keyword — `cpp/override-signature-aware` is the control that proves it, because a control that only runs in the upgraded direction proves nothing about the direction that costs confidence.

expectRelationships.note: M14-HONESTY-CONTRACT §4: an edge at 1.0 needs no reason code for the confidence itself, but the reason code records HOW it was established, and `overrideSpecifier` records that the author wrote the keyword. Both are the difference between this edge and the 0.9 inference its predecessor was.
